opportunities.title: Synthesis Grants

amount.raw: Synthesis groups can claim up to £30,000 over two years

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Main applicant must have BES membership; working groups of 8-15 participants with diverse mix of career stages, institutions and international participation; groups should not be formed entirely of academic institution members.
opportunities.summary: Fast-tracking innovative and impactful research by contributing up to £30k towards the formation of new two-year synthesis groups that bring together diverse interdisciplinary groups to analyse and synthesise existing data.

opportunities.title: Long-Term Research Grants

amount.raw: £500 per year for a decade; £3,500 for first five years claimed in year 1, with an additional £3,500 claimable in year six

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; awarded to individuals, not organisations; open to all types of ecologists including conservation practitioners, reserve managers, consultants and university academics.
opportunities.summary: Provides a small amount of funding each year for 10 years to enable existing short-term projects with at least 1-2 years of data to be funded into the long term, supporting long-term ecological studies anywhere in the world.

opportunities.title: Pedagogical Research and Development Grants

amount.raw: Projects can be awarded up to £5,000

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to anyone involved in teaching ecology at any level; projects max 12 months; awarded to individuals, not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Improving the education of future generations of ecologists by funding research on ecology teaching and learning practices, providing up to £5k towards evidence-based learning.

opportunities.title: Connecting Ecologists with Other Disciplines Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to PhD students, postdoctoral fellows, early career ecologists, established researchers or employees of other organisations; undergraduates and masters students not eligible; awarded to individuals.
opportunities.summary: Promoting interdisciplinary skills by funding up to £20k towards placements (secondments) in different disciplines and sectors, up to 12 months, to immerse an ecologist in another professional world.

opportunities.title: Small Research Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Funding provided for researchers from all countries globally; projects can be conducted anywhere in the world; BES membership required; not a scholarship.
opportunities.summary: Providing up to £5,000 for new and innovative ecological research of the highest international standard, with a clear ecological science focus.

opportunities.title: Outreach and Engagement Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Lead applicant must have BES membership; open to individuals, teams and organisations across all experience levels; projects max 12 months; proposals must target a non-academic audience.
opportunities.summary: Providing funding of up to £2,000 for individuals, teams and organisations to engage public audiences with the excitement of ecological science through outreach, public engagement and science communication.

opportunities.title: Training and Travel Grants

amount.raw: A maximum of £500 is available for events in person; a maximum of £250 is available to cover registration fees for virtual conferences/courses

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member; must be a PhD student or postgraduate researcher (postdocs, undergraduates and masters students not eligible); must work or study at a university or research institution; must give a presentation if attending a meeting.
opportunities.summary: Helps PhD students and postgraduate researchers meet the costs of specialist field training courses and the travel costs associated with presenting their work at workshops and conferences.

opportunities.title: Annual Meeting Grants 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member at any career stage; must be a citizen of and based in the Global South; must be travelling from and returning to that country; must have applied to present at the Annual Meeting; must be at least three years since last BES Training and Travel Grant.
opportunities.summary: Supports researchers based in Global South countries to attend the BES Annual Meeting in the UK, covering costs directly related to attending the meeting such as registration, transport, food and accommodation.
